495	    /// Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes
496	    #[command(long_about = format!("Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.\n\n\
497	        Repo set is resolved (in order):\n  \
498	          - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)\n  \
499	          - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`\n  \
500	          - neither             `.`, the one repo sync is run in\n\n\
501	        Safe by default: before it fetches, sync finds out what the\n\
502	        fetch would do. It asks the remote where its bookmarks are,\n\
503	        downloads the commits of those that moved without moving a\n\
504	        ref, and tells a fast-forward from a rewrite. Then:\n  \
505	          - remote has not moved   nothing to fetch\n  \
506	          - only fast-forwarded    fetch; local work is left untouched\n  \
507	          - would tangle           held back; sync says why, exits non-zero\n\
508	        A fetch would tangle local work when a bookmark that moved has\n\
509	        local commits of its own, or when the remote rewrote a\n\
510	        bookmark and the repo holds local work: uncommitted changes in\n\
511	        `@` (not asked of the agent repo, whose `@` holds the running\n\
512	        session), an `@-` that is not on the remote, or a bookmark\n\
513	        with commits the remote does not have. --force, or --rebase,\n\
514	        syncs a repo that would be held back.\n\n\
515	        With --dry-run sync does the same finding out and stops: it\n\
516	        reports each repo's state, its local work, and what a sync\n\
517	        would do, and moves no bookmark, `@`, or remote-tracking ref.\n\
518	        It exits 0 whatever it finds.\n\n\
519	        One atomic operation: fetch, then per repo, by where its\n\
520	        bookmark was before the fetch:\n  \
521	          - up-to-date        nothing to do\n  \
522	          - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote\n  \
523	          - rewritten         the remote replaced the commit; fetch followed it\n  \
524	          - ahead             nothing to sync\n  \
525	          - diverged          --force only: rebase onto remote, fail on conflicts\n  \
526	          - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip\n\n\
527	        After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced\n\
528	        bookmark: the work repo `jj new`s a clean `@` (or with\n\
529	        --force rebases a dirty one), the `.claude` session repo\n\
530	        `jj new main`s when main moved (no-op when `@-` is already\n\
531	        the main tip).\n\n\
532	        On failure sync stops where the failing step stopped: nothing\n\
533	        is auto-reverted, so the state can be inspected. The failure\n\
534	        report prints each repo's pre-sync op id; undo explicitly with\n\
535	        `jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing persists across\n\
536	        invocations.\n\n\
537	        Output shape:\n  \
538	          - all-up-to-date: one-line summary (`sync: N repos are {}`)\n  \
539	          - anything else:  per-repo fetch + state + actions\n  \
540	          - --quiet:        no output; exit code signals success", sync::UP_TO_DATE_MSG))]

552	        A push that would be forced, the target already on the\n\
553	        bookmark's remote or the remote not below it, asks before\n\
554	        anything changes, so a published commit is rewritten only by\n\
555	        choice. The --yes flag answers in advance, a configured\n\
556	        squash-push.yes never does, and without a tty and --yes it is\n\
557	        an error.\n\n\
558	        Zero-ceremony default: bare `vc-x1 squash-push` squashes\n\
559	        @ -> @- in `.` and pushes the bookmark of the line you are\n\
560	        on. With an empty `@` but work still to do, the squash is\n\
561	        skipped and the push still runs.\n\n\
562	        --bookmark defaults to the line's own bookmark, the nearest one\n\
563	        at or above the squash target, and there is no literal\n\
564	        default. On the agent repo that is `main`. On a work repo\n\

794	/// Permanent sanity check for the `main`-bookmark tracking state
795	/// in both repos of the dual-repo workspace. Emits one line on
796	/// entry and one on exit of every command. If entry and exit
797	/// differ, the executing command is the culprit. If entry differs
798	/// from the previous command's exit, something *between*
799	/// invocations broke it. Originally added in 0.37.2 as a temporary
800	/// diagnostic. Promoted to permanent in 0.37.4 after the user
801	/// reported "happens more than once".
802	///
803	/// Emits at `log::debug!` (since 0.52.0-1): default runs stay
804	/// quiet, and the signal remains available under `-v` when
805	/// investigating.
806	///
807	/// Walks up from cwd to locate the workspace root (the directory
808	/// whose `.vc-config.toml` has a `work` key), then probes `<root>`
809	/// and the config-resolved bot dir. Same labeling whether the user
810	/// runs from the work root, from the bot dir, or from any subdir.
811	pub fn bm_track(phase: &str, command_name: &str) {
812	    let header = format!("bm-track {phase} vc-x1 {command_name}");
813	    let root = match common::find_workspace_root() {
814	        Some(r) => r,
815	        None => {
816	            log::debug!("{header}: no-workspace");
817	            return;
818	        }
819	    };
820	    // Diagnostics only: an unresolvable / single-repo workspace
821	    // just probes the work side.
822	    let mut repos: Vec<(std::path::PathBuf, String)> = vec![(root.clone(), "work".to_string())];
823	    if let Ok(Some(bot)) = common::bot_repo_path(&root) {
824	        let label = bot
825	            .file_name()
826	            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
827	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "agent".to_string());
828	        repos.push((bot, label));
829	    }
830	    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
831	    for (repo, label) in repos {
832	        if !repo.join(".jj").exists() {
833	            parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=no-jj"));
834	            continue;
835	        }
836	        match bm_track_one(&repo, "main", "origin") {
837	            Ok(true) => parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=tracked")),
838	            Ok(false) => parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=NOT_TRACKED")),
839	            Err(e) => parts.push(format!(
840	                "{label}(main)=err({})",
841	                e.lines().next().unwrap_or("")
842	            )),
843	        }
844	    }
845	    log::debug!("{header}: {}", parts.join(", "));
846	}

848	/// Query whether `bookmark` in `repo` is tracking `remote`.
849	/// Returns `Ok(true)` when a present, tracked remote ref exists
850	/// (synced or divergent, both count), `Ok(false)` when it doesn't
851	/// (not tracking, or the bookmark doesn't exist). The typed view
852	/// query (`jj::has_tracked_remote`) replaced the CLI-listing
853	/// parser family here.
854	fn bm_track_one(repo: &Path, bookmark: &str, remote: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
855	    jj::has_tracked_remote(repo, bookmark, remote).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
856	}

858	fn main() -> ExitCode {
859	    run_cmd::forward_completion();
860	    CompleteEnv::with_factory(cli_with_banner).complete();
861	    let matches = cli_with_banner().get_matches();
862	    let cli = match Cli::from_arg_matches(&matches) {
863	        Ok(cli) => cli,
864	        Err(e) => {
865	            e.exit();
866	        }
867	    };
868	
869	    let log_path = cli.log.as_ref().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string());
870	    logging::CliLogger::init(cli.verbose, log_path.as_deref());
871	
872	    // Version output rides along with every run so any captured
873	    // output says which version produced it. Stream by who asked:
874	    // `-V`/`-VV` are explicit requests, so they go to stdout where
875	    // a script capturing output collects them. Unasked-for
876	    // provenance goes to stderr, keeping stdout parseable for the
877	    // commands that emit data there. The `version` subcommand
878	    // prints the report itself, so it skips all of this. Uniform
879	    // `BANNER` (not the `vc-x1-<sub>` form clap's
880	    // `propagate_version` would print): the version is the
881	    // binary's regardless of which subcommand it routes to.
882	    //
883	    // `eprintln!` rather than the logger because `CliLogger` puts
884	    // info on stdout by level. The cost is that `--log` does not
885	    // capture the ambient banner.
886	    let version_cmd = matches!(cli.command, Some(Commands::Version));
887	    if !version_cmd {
888	        match cli.version {
889	            0 => {
890	                // Skip the ambient banner when no subcommand was
891	                // given: that path prints help, whose about line
892	                // opens with the same banner text, and the pair
893	                // read as a stuttered header (seen dogfooding the
894	                // argv0 banner, 2026-08-06).
895	                if !cli.no_banner && cli.command.is_some() {
896	                    eprintln!("{}", run_banner());
897	                }
898	            }
899	            1 => log::info!("{}", run_banner()),
900	            _ => {
901	                for line in version::report(banner()) {
902	                    log::info!("{line}");
903	                }
904	            }
905	        }
906	    }
907	
908	    let Some(cmd) = cli.command else {
909	        // No subcommand. If `-V` was set the banner or report has
910	        // already printed, so exit success. Otherwise mirror
911	        // clap's "a subcommand is required" error by printing
912	        // usage and exiting non-zero.
913	        if cli.version > 0 {
914	            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
915	        }
916	        let mut cmd = cli_with_banner();
917	        let _ = cmd.print_help();
918	        return ExitCode::FAILURE;
919	    };
920	
921	    // Answered before `Context::load`, which needs a workspace:
922	    // the versions that describe a run are exactly what you want
923	    // when the workspace is what's broken.
924	    if let Commands::Version = cmd {
925	        for line in version::report(banner()) {
926	            log::info!("{line}");
927	        }
928	        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
929	    }
930	
931	    // The run record every operation this process commits carries,
932	    // begun before any repo is opened, the program named as the
933	    // banner names it.
934	    jj::run::begin_run(banner());
935	
936	    // The version gate: every subcommand, no exceptions beyond
937	    // `version`, which returned above. Not scoped to the write path,
938	    // because "read" in jj-lib means "writes nothing the caller
939	    // asked for": `load_at_head` merges divergent op heads, the
940	    // index self-heals by rewriting segments, and an `@`-relative
941	    // read snapshots the working copy.
942	    //
943	    // Nor scoped to a list of repo-touching commands. Such a list
944	    // enforces only its own completeness: a command that grows a
945	    // repo read later stays classified as safe, silently. `--help`
946	    // and shell completion need no exempting, having exited inside
947	    // clap and `CompleteEnv` before this point. See
948	    // notes/jj-version-policy.md.
949	    if !cli.allow_jj_mismatch
950	        && let Err(e) = version::gate()
951	    {
952	        error!("{e}");
953	        return ExitCode::FAILURE;
954	    }
955	
956	    // Reads a directory listing, never a repo, and must answer in a
957	    // plain old repo too, so it runs after the gate and before
958	    // `Context::load`.
959	    if let Commands::AgentFiles(args) = &cmd {
960	        return args.run();
961	    }
962	
963	    let mut ctx = match context::Context::load() {
964	        Ok(c) => c,
965	        Err(e) => {
966	            error!("{e}");
967	            return ExitCode::FAILURE;
968	        }
969	    };
970	
971	    match cmd {
972	        // Handled above, before `Context::load`.
973	        Commands::Version | Commands::AgentFiles(_) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
974	        Commands::Chid(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
975	        Commands::Desc(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
976	        Commands::List(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
977	        Commands::Show(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
978	        Commands::Status(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
979	        Commands::Lookup(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
980	        Commands::BotSession(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
981	        Commands::BotSessionOld { .. } => {
982	            error!(
983	                "bot-session: pre-0.80.0 name. The agent side is `agent`, so the \
984	                 subcommand is `agent-session` (same flags)."
985	            );
986	            ExitCode::FAILURE
987	        }
988	        Commands::Validate(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
989	        Commands::Build(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
990	        Commands::BuildDev(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
991	        Commands::Install(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
992	        Commands::InstallDev(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
993	        Commands::Run(args) => run_cmd::dispatch(run_cmd::RunParams::try_from(&args)),
994	        Commands::RunDev(args) => run_cmd::dispatch(run_cmd::RunParams::try_from(&args)),
995	        Commands::ValidateBot(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
996	        Commands::ValidateBotOld { .. } => {
997	            error!(
998	                "validate-bot: pre-0.80.0 name. The agent side is `agent`, so the \
999	                 subcommand is `validate-agent` (same flags)."
1000	            );
1001	            ExitCode::FAILURE
1002	        }
1003	        Commands::ValidateDesc(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1004	        Commands::FixDesc(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1005	        Commands::ValidateConfig(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1006	        Commands::ValidateAnchors(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1007	        Commands::ValidateTodo(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1008	        Commands::FixTodo(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1009	        Commands::Clone(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1010	        Commands::Init(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1011	        Commands::Symlink(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1012	        Commands::Sync(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1013	        Commands::SquashPush(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1014	        Commands::Config(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1015	        Commands::Push(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1016	        Commands::Commit(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1017	        Commands::Squash(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),
1018	        Commands::Merge(args) => args.dispatch(&mut ctx),

# vc-x1 config file

Configure the work-repo of a dual repo system. The other repo, we call the agent-repo, is
also a markdown configuration file typically named .vc-config.md.

The code blocks in these config files are in toml format and these blocks are logically
concatenated in the order written here and those become the information used for configuring
the system. The [vc-config.md](vc-config.md) contains the documentation for the
various toml tables used for configuration and it is also used during compilation to define
the valid contents of this file.

The file [vc-config-model.md](vc-config-model.md) is the model: every table and key a workspace
config may carry, each with its default or a typical value. It is generated from the schema, so it
cannot fall behind the keys the binary knows.

The two repos
- work [[1]]
- agent [[2]]
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".agent-session"
```

The agent-repo's name on its remote, which clone and sync need when there is no agent-repo yet to
ask
- agent-repo [[9]]
```toml
[remote]
agent-repo = "vc-x1.agent-session"
```

The agent-file family this repo belongs to: its member name and the sibling repos it answers to
- member [[3]]
- template [[4]]
- messages [[5]]
```toml
[family]
member = "vc-x1"
template = "../vc-x1-template/work"
messages = "../vc-x1-messages"
```

The validation commands, each element one invocation, run in order by `vc-x1 validate`
- full [[6]]
- fast [[7]], `cargo test --bins` alone, the schema's example, wink's call 2026-10-20: the full
  list with plain `cargo test` measured the same 8 s as full, since the fourteen `dr1_*` fixture
  tests cost nothing once the fixture is built, so the only fast worth having skips fmt, clippy,
  the integration tests, and the install. Its trial of 2026-09-21 found a rung's failures in what
  it skips, so a rung's review still runs full
- full checks the source and makes no build to run, wink's call 2026-10-21: the dev build is
  `[build] dev` below, which `vc-x1 run --dev` runs first, so what runs is always the current code,
  and the test build full leaves is what the dev build then reuses
```toml
[validate]
full = [
  "cargo fmt",
  "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings",
  "cargo test -- --include-ignored",
]
fast = ["cargo test --bins"]
```

The build, one list for every profile, run in order with each element one invocation, a plain
`cargo build` naming the chosen profile's `Cargo.toml` profile, so its binary stays in `target/`
and nothing on the PATH is replaced until `vc-x1 install` copies it there, and `--locked` so every
profile's build compiles the same dependencies
- commands [[10]], the build, run by `vc-x1 build` and first by `vc-x1 run` and `vc-x1 install`,
  `{profile.cargo}` filled from the profile `--profile` names, else the default [[19]], release
```toml
[build]
commands = ["cargo build --profile {profile.cargo} --locked"]
```

The install, one list for every profile, written out so the config says what `vc-x1 install` does.
It copies the binary to a `.new` file and then moves it into place, since a copy onto a running
binary fails and a move swaps it in whole, so a copy already running keeps the old code and the
next run gets the new. The list uses `{table.key}` placeholders, filled for the run, so each path
is written once, and `~` is expanded to the home directory, so the value fits every machine.

# vc-x1 config file

Configure the work-repo of a dual repo system. The other repo, we call the agent-repo, is
also a markdown configuration file typically named .vc-config.md.

The code blocks in these config files are in toml format and these blocks are logically
concatenated in the order written here and those become the information used for configuring
the system. The [vc-config.md](vc-config.md) contains the documentation for the
various toml tables used for configuration and it is also used during compilation to define
the valid contents of this file.

The file [vc-config-model.md](vc-config-model.md) is the model: every table and key a workspace
config may carry, each with its default or a typical value. It is generated from the schema, so it
cannot fall behind the keys the binary knows.

[repos]

agent = ".agent-session"

agent-repo = "vc-x1.agent-session"

1	//! The `commit` subcommand: make a rung's commit pair, one commit
2	//! per repo of a dual workspace, each stamped with the other's
3	//! change id, before anything is pushed.
4	//!
5	//! The pair is what the per-rung flow reviews: the description and
6	//! the diff together, as a commit, by `vc-x1 show -s both @-`.
7	//! Nothing here reaches a remote, so a fix after the review is a
8	//! fold into the pair and never a remote rewrite, and `vc-x1 push`
9	//! has nothing left to write: it publishes what was reviewed.
10	//!
11	//! - `-s b` makes both commits now. Both change ids are known
12	//!   before either is made, since a jj commit keeps the working
13	//!   copy's change id, so each trailer is written once and never
14	//!   predicted or restamped.
15	//! - `-s w` makes the work commit now, its trailer naming the agent
16	//!   `@` all the same, and leaves the agent half to `push`, which
17	//!   commits the journal as the partner. The pair is then made in
18	//!   two steps, and the review's own transcript lands in the rung's
19	//!   agent commit.
20	//! - A trailer holds the partner's change id, and with an `origin`
21	//!   each half names the other's repo by `orepo:` above it. Neither
22	//!   holds a SHA, so `-s w`'s trailers are final before the agent
23	//!   commit is made.
24	//! - `-s a` commits the agent repo alone, an unpaired commit with the
25	//!   given title and body and no trailer, since it belongs to no
26	//!   rung. An agent `@` that is a work commit's pending partner keeps
27	//!   its change id when committed, so the work commit's trailer still
28	//!   resolves, and a warning says the back-trailer is missing.
29	//! - The commit is pushed in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push`
30	//!   would after it, when asked: a pair by `push -s b`, its agent half completed
31	//!   as the partner and its bookmark published, a plain repo by
32	//!   `push -s p`, and an agent commit by publishing the agent `main`.
33	//!   Only with `--push`: a commit otherwise stays on the machine,
34	//!   `--opening`'s bookmark included, which `--local`, or its alias
35	//!   `--no-push`, says outright.
36	//! - `-s p` commits a plain repo with the title and body and no
37	//!   trailer, the same description discipline on a repo with no
38	//!   partner.
39	//! - `--body` is the text, or `@PATH` to read it from a file, since
40	//!   a body in commit-body form has markers and blank lines a shell
41	//!   quote mangles.
42	//! - The work side's `@` must hold a change, since a rung changes
43	//!   the work repo. The agent side's `@` is the session's journal
44	//!   and is committed as it stands.
45	//! - `REV`, the positional, is the commit the description is for:
46	//!   `@` by default, committed as above, else `@-` or any draft below
47	//!   it, described in place with no new commit, its trailer stamped,
48	//!   so a commit made by hand becomes a rung's. The draft must be
49	//!   unpublished, no remote bookmark reaching it, carry no trailer
50	//!   yet, and hold a change, so the describe is a draft's rewrite and
51	//!   never a re-describe. `@` is left as it is, as `push` leaves new
52	//!   work, and a draft below `@-` is committed and not pushed, since
53	//!   push publishes `@-`. Not with `--opening` or `--closing`, whose
54	//!   commits are made from `@`.
55	//! - `--closing <BM|REV>` closes the cycle whose tip the argument
56	//!   names, a bookmark or a revision as jj resolves them, required,
57	//!   onto `--onto`'s bookmark, also required, since no target is
58	//!   assumed. It is read where it is now, so a target that moved
59	//!   during the cycle is joined by the merge, and left out it is
60	//!   refused naming the likely one:
61	//!   - One commit above the target, the opening: a single-step cycle,
62	//!     finalized in place, no new commit. `@` folds into it when it
63	//!     sits on it, it takes the bare cycle title, its body and
64	//!     trailer kept, and the agent `@` is left for push, since the
65	//!     commit's partner is the opening's.
66	//!   - More: the closing commit, the target and the tip as its parents
67	//!     in that order, by the primitive `vc-x1 merge` uses, carrying
68	//!     the record move and, when the tip is `@-`, what `@` holds.
69	//!     `--dead-end` always makes it.
70	//!   - A tip that is not `@-`, any commit on any line: `@` moves
71	//!     onto it first and returns after, to the same commit when it
72	//!     held work and to a fresh empty one on its parent when it did
73	//!     not, so the closing is made from the tip's working copy and
74	//!     the user's line is as it was, the commits above the tip
75	//!     included, their line unclosed.
76	//!   - `--title` is the bare cycle title, read from the opening, the
77	//!     first commit above the target, when left out, and " closing" is
78	//!     appended, " dead-end closing" with `--dead-end`. `--body`
79	//!     defaults to `[closing] body`, its `{title}` the cycle title,
80	//!     and a finalized commit keeps the opening's.
81	//! - `--opening <BOOKMARK>` makes the work commit the cycle's
82	//!   opening: `--title` is the bare cycle title and " opening" is
83	//!   appended. The bookmark, the one named or the title's slug, is
84	//!   `vc-x1 open`'s, made first on the work `@`, so it follows the
85	//!   change into the opening, and the opening creates none: one missing
86	//!   is refused before the commit, naming `vc-x1 open`. It stays local
87	//!   like the rest unless `--push` asks, a rung's push.
88	//! - The line's bookmark advances to the work commit, locally: the
89	//!   nearest bookmark below the work `@-`, as `push` resolves it, or
90	//!   the one `--bookmark` names, any on the line at or below the work
91	//!   commit, so the cycle's bookmark follows a rung past a nearer one
92	//!   of the user's, or `--opening`'s. jj moves a bookmark
93	//!   with its commit through a later squash or amend, so the advance
94	//!   holds through the review's fixes, and the remote moves only at
95	//!   `push`. `--no-advance` leaves it, and none or several candidates
96	//!   are refused before anything is made. The agent repo's `main` is
97	//!   push's to set.
98	//! - A failure after the first commit restores both repos from the
99	//!   `jj op` snapshots taken just before it, as push does inside its
100	//!   mutation window.

119	/// Commit the working copies as a rung's pair, or a plain repo's
120	/// commit, with the given title and body.
121	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
122	pub struct CommitArgs {
123	    /// Retired: the revision, now `-r`, refused naming it.
124	    #[arg(value_name = "RETIRED", hide = true)]
125	    pub retired: Option<String>,
126	
127	    /// The commit the description is for: `@` by default, committed as
128	    /// the working copy; `@-` or any draft below it is described in
129	    /// place with no new commit, its trailer stamped, so a commit made
130	    /// by hand becomes a rung's. Not with `--opening` or `--closing`
131	    #[arg(
132	        short = 'r',
133	        long = "revision",
134	        value_name = "REV",

375	impl TryFrom<&CommitArgs> for CommitParams {
376	    type Error = String;
377	
378	    /// Resolve the scope into its repos, refusing the agent half
379	    /// alone, read the body when it names a file, and check the
380	    /// description is not blank.
381	    fn try_from(a: &CommitArgs) -> Result<Self, String> {
382	        // `--land <TRUNK>` took a value before the target became
383	        // `--onto`'s, so a value after `--land` is that form, not the
384	        // retired revision positional.
385	        if let (Some(value), true) = (&a.retired, a.land) {
386	            return Err(format!(
387	                "commit --land: it takes no value now, the target being --onto's: `--onto {value} \
388	                 --land`"
389	            ));
390	        }
391	        if let Some(value) = &a.retired {
392	            return Err(crate::options_flags::retired_positional::refusal(
393	                "commit", value, "-r",
394	            ));
395	        }
396	        if a.opening.is_some() && a.no_advance {
397	            return Err(
398	                "commit --opening: its bookmark is on the opening already, made by \
399	                        `vc-x1 open`, so --no-advance moves nothing"
400	                    .into(),
401	            );
402	        }
403	        if a.rev.is_some() && (a.opening.is_some() || a.closing.is_some()) {
404	            return Err(
405	                "commit -r: a bookend is made from `@`, so -r takes neither \
406	                        --opening nor --closing"
407	                    .into(),
408	            );
409	        }
410	        if a.covers.is_some() && !matches!(&a.scope, RepoScope::Sides(s) if s.is_bot_only()) {
411	            return Err(
412	                "commit --covers: the work commits an agent commit covers, so it takes -s a".into(),
413	            );
414	        }
415	        if a.rev.is_some() && matches!(&a.scope, RepoScope::Sides(s) if s.is_bot_only()) {
416	            return Err(
417	                "commit -s a: -r is the work commit's, so the agent repo alone takes none".into(),
418	            );
419	        }
420	        let body = match &a.body {
421	            Some(b) => Some(crate::desc_helpers::read_body(b, "commit")?),
422	            None => None,
423	        };
424	        if a.title.as_deref().is_some_and(|t| t.trim().is_empty())
425	            || body.as_deref().is_some_and(|b| b.trim().is_empty())
426	        {
427	            return Err("commit: --title and --body must both be non-empty".into());
428	        }
429	        let target = match &a.scope {
430	            RepoScope::Por => {
431	                let repos = crate::common::resolve_scoped_repos(&a.scope, a.repo.as_deref())
432	                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
433	                match repos.as_slice() {
434	                    [repo] => Target::Por(repo.clone()),
435	                    other => {
436	                        return Err(format!(
437	                            "commit -s p: expected one repo, got {}",
438	                            other.len()
439	                        ));
440	                    }
441	                }
442	            }
443	            RepoScope::Sides(sides) => {
444	                // Both paths whatever the side, since `w` needs the
445	                // agent @'s change id for its trailer.
446	                let pair = resolve_pair(a.repo.as_deref()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
447	                if sides.is_bot_only() {
448	                    if a.opening.is_some() || a.closing.is_some() {
449	                        return Err("commit -s a: a bookend is the work repo's, so `--opening` \
450	                                    and `--closing` take `-s b` or `-s w`"
451	                            .into());
452	                    }
453	                    Target::Agent(pair)
454	                } else {
455	                    Target::Pair {
456	                        pair,
457	                        agent_now: sides.is_both(),
458	                    }
459	                }
460	            }
461	        };
462	        let (title, opening) = match (&a.opening, &a.title) {
463	            (Some(named), Some(t)) => (
464	                Some(opening_title(t)?),
465	                Some(Opening {
466	                    bookmark: opening_bookmark(named.as_deref(), t)?,
467	                }),
468	            ),
469	            (Some(_), None) => return Err("commit --opening: --title is required".into()),
470	            (None, t) => (t.clone(), None),
471	        };
472	        if a.closing.is_some()
473	            && let Some(t) = &title
474	        {
475	            refuse_suffixed(t, "--closing")?;
476	        }
477	        Ok(CommitParams {
478	            target,
479	            title,
480	            body,
481	            closing: a.closing.as_ref().map(|rev| Closing {
482	                rev: rev.clone(),
483	                dead_end: a.dead_end,
484	                onto: a.onto.clone(),
485	            }),
486	            opening,
487	            advance: match (&a.bookmark, a.no_advance) {
488	                (_, true) => Advance::Off,
489	                (Some(b), false) => Advance::Named(b.clone()),
490	                (None, false) => Advance::Line,
491	            },
492	            land: a.land,
493	            skip: a.skip,
494	            push: a.push,
495	            no_url_trailer: a.no_url_trailer,
496	            dry_run: a.dry_run.value,
497	            rev: a.rev.clone(),
498	            covers: a.covers.clone(),
499	        })
500	    }
501	}

517	/// Entry point: the pair, or the plain commit, a closing's detour
518	/// around either.
519	pub fn commit(ctx: &mut Context, params: &CommitParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
520	    debug!("commit: enter {params:?}");
521	    match &params.target {
522	        Target::Pair { pair, agent_now } => {
523	            let now = *agent_now;
524	            with_detour(ctx, &pair.work, params, |ctx| {
525	                commit_pair(ctx, pair, now, params)
526	            })
527	        }
528	        Target::Por(repo) => with_detour(ctx, repo, params, |ctx| commit_por(ctx, repo, params)),
529	        Target::Agent(pair) => commit_agent(ctx, pair, params),
530	    }
531	}

533	/// How `@` returns from a closing's detour: a fresh empty commit on
534	/// the parent it had, when it was discardable and the move abandoned
535	/// it, or an edit of the same commit, which the move kept. Both by
536	/// change id, since a finalize rewrites the tip and rebases the
537	/// commits above it, giving them new commit ids.
538	enum Back {
539	    NewOn(String),
540	    Edit(String),
541	}
542	
543	/// Run a commit, with `@` moved onto the closing's tip first when the
544	/// tip is not `@-` and returned after, so the closing is made from
545	/// the tip's working copy and the user's line is as it was. The move
546	/// is undone with the rest on a failure, and a dry run moves nothing
547	/// and says so.
548	fn with_detour(
549	    ctx: &mut Context,
550	    repo: &Path,
551	    params: &CommitParams,
552	    run: impl FnOnce(&mut Context) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>,
553	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
554	    let Some(c) = &params.closing else {
555	        return run(ctx);
556	    };
557	    let tip = resolve_closing(repo, &c.rev)?;
558	    // `@` itself is a branch with nothing committed, closed from `@`.
559	    if jj::matches(repo, &format!("{tip} & (@ | @-)"))? {
560	        return run(ctx);
561	    }
562	    if params.dry_run {
563	        info!(
564	            "commit: [dry-run] '{}' is not the work @-, so @ would move onto it first and \
565	             return after; what follows reads the branch at @-",
566	            c.rev
567	        );
568	        return run(ctx);
569	    }
570	    crate::pair::refuse_conflicts(repo, "commit", "work")?;
571	    let discardable = jj::is_empty(repo, "@")?
572	        && jj::desc_of(repo, "@")?.trim().is_empty()
573	        && jj::local_bookmarks_at(repo, "@")?.is_empty();
574	    let back = if discardable {
575	        Back::NewOn(jj::chid_of(repo, "@-")?)
576	    } else {
577	        Back::Edit(jj::chid_of(repo, "@")?)
578	    };
579	    let snapshot = crate::pair::Snapshot::take(repo)?;
580	    info!(
581	        "commit --closing: '{}' is not the work @-, so @ moves onto it, and returns after",
582	        c.rev
583	    );
584	    if let Err(e) = ctx.session(repo)?.new_on(&tip) {
585	        snapshot.restore("commit", e.as_ref());
586	        return Err(e);
587	    }
588	    if let Err(e) = run(ctx) {
589	        snapshot.restore("commit", e.as_ref());
590	        return Err(e);
591	    }
592	    let returned = match &back {
593	        Back::NewOn(parent) => ctx.session(repo)?.new_on(parent),
594	        Back::Edit(chid) => ctx.session(repo)?.edit(chid),
595	    };
596	    returned.map_err(|e| {
597	        format!("commit --closing: the closing is made, and @ did not return to where it was: {e}")
598	            .into()
599	    })
600	}

602	/// The draft `REV` names, described in place: the revision as given.
603	#[derive(Debug)]
604	struct Draft {
605	    rev: String,
606	}

608	/// Resolve `REV` to the draft it names, `None` for `@` or when no
609	/// REV was given, refusing before anything is made: a revset that is
610	/// not one commit, a published commit, whose describe would be a
611	/// remote rewrite, one that carries a trailer already, so is a pair's
612	/// commit and `squash --title --body` re-describes it, a conflicted
613	/// one, and an empty one, since a rung changes the repo.
614	fn plan_draft(
615	    repo: &Path,
616	    params: &CommitParams,
617	) -> Result<Option<Draft>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
618	    let Some(rev) = &params.rev else {
619	        return Ok(None);
620	    };
621	    let cids = jj::cids_of(repo, rev)
622	        .map_err(|e| format!("commit REV: '{rev}' in {}: {e}", repo.display()))?;
623	    if cids.len() != 1 {
624	        return Err(format!(
625	            "commit REV: '{rev}' names {} commits in {}, and the description is one commit's",
626	            cids.len(),
627	            repo.display()
628	        )
629	        .into());
630	    }
631	    if jj::matches(repo, &format!("({rev}) & @"))? {
632	        return Ok(None);
633	    }
634	    if crate::pair::is_published(repo, rev)? {
635	        return Err(format!(
636	            "commit REV: '{rev}' is published, an ancestor of a remote bookmark in {}, so \
637	             describing it is a remote rewrite",
638	            repo.display()
639	        )
640	        .into());
641	    }
642	    if crate::desc_helpers::extract_ochid_from_desc(&jj::desc_of(repo, rev)?).is_some() {
643	        return Err(format!(
644	            "commit REV: '{rev}' carries an `ochid:` trailer already, so it is a pair's commit: \
645	             `vc-x1 squash --title --body` re-describes it"
646	        )
647	        .into());
648	    }
649	    if jj::matches(repo, &format!("({rev}) & conflicts()"))? {
650	        return Err(format!("commit REV: '{rev}' is conflicted, so it is not described").into());
651	    }
652	    if jj::is_empty(repo, rev)? {
653	        return Err(format!(
654	            "commit REV: nothing to describe, '{rev}' is empty in {}",
655	            repo.display()
656	        )
657	        .into());
658	    }
659	    Ok(Some(Draft { rev: rev.clone() }))
660	}

662	/// Refuse a repo that cannot take the commit: a conflicted one, or
663	/// for the work side an empty `@`, since a rung changes the work
664	/// repo and an empty commit would carry a trailer naming nothing
665	/// worth reviewing. A closing is never refused for an empty `@`,
666	/// since the merge is its content.
667	fn preflight(
668	    repo: &Path,
669	    label: &str,
670	    must_change: bool,
671	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
672	    crate::pair::refuse_conflicts(repo, "commit", label)?;
673	    if must_change && jj::is_empty(repo, "@")? {
674	        return Err(format!(
675	            "commit: nothing to commit, the {label} repo's @ is empty ('{}')",
676	            repo.display()
677	        )
678	        .into());
679	    }
680	    Ok(())
681	}

683	/// Make the pair: both change ids read from the working copies
684	/// first, then the work commit with the agent's id in its trailer
685	/// and, with `agent_now`, the agent commit with the work's id in
686	/// its own. Without it the agent `@` is left for push to commit as
687	/// the partner, its id already in the work commit's trailer.
688	fn commit_pair(
689	    ctx: &mut Context,
690	    pair: &Pair,
691	    agent_now: bool,
692	    params: &CommitParams,
693	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
694	    let (work, agent) = (pair.work.as_path(), pair.agent.as_path());
695	    let closing = plan_closing(work, params)?;
696	    let tip = closing_tip(closing.as_ref()).to_string();
697	    let closing_bm = closing_bookmark(work, params, closing.as_ref(), &tip)?;
698	    let land = plan_land(work, params, &tip, closing_bm.as_deref())?;
699	    // A Land commits the agent `@`, naming every commit that names it,
700	    // the closing among them.
701	    let agent_now = agent_now && land.is_none();

content.content:
## Todo format

`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
reference links to more detail.

- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
- `## Ideas`: unranked.
- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
  numbering](#reference-numbering)).

Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
project's record, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.

An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

Example shape:

```
## Todo

### Add new feature X

The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **rungs**: a `#### Rungs` heading over the rung subsections, the ladder itself being `zTOC.md`'s
  ([zTOC format](#ztoc-format)): one rung per step, `- 2 (done) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: the
  rung's version suffix, which `-V` and the installed dev build print, then the marker, `(done)` or
  `(current)`, both first so they read down their columns, and a rung not yet started has neither,
  its suffix being set when its commit bumps the version, and an inline link so the ladder is one
  list with nothing beside it to keep in step, its line as long as the title makes it. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per [Conventional-commit
  shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved `## Todo` entry is retitled.
  The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

A rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title
links to the rung's subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## zTOC format

`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
in a listing. Its sections, in this order:

- `# TOC`, the title.
- `## Ladder`: the cycle's ladder, its one copy, each rung with its marker as [The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block) shapes it, linking across to its subsection in `TODO.md`, since a
  same-file link does not work in every markdown preview, zed's among them. Written at the opening,
  replacing the last cycle's, its markers set by the per-rung flow, and kept by the closing commit,
  so the landmark's tree holds the finished ladder beside its `## Closed`.
- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first.

Its links are inline, so it has no `# References`.

Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
Ladder` reading `_None._` until the first opening.

## Frozen history: chores and done
# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.


## zTOC.md's ladder

The same cycle's ladder, `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`, its one copy, linking across to the subsections
above:

```
## Ladder

- 0 (done) [refactor: extract config loader opening](TODO.md#refactor-extract-config-loader-opening)
- 1 (current) [refactor: split loader from parser](TODO.md#refactor-split-loader-from-parser)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing](TODO.md#refactor-extract-config-loader-closing)
```

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

`-R` is optional and says where. `--body` is the text, or `@PATH` to read it from a file, since a
body in commit-body form has markers and blank lines a shell quote mangles. The work repo's `@`
must hold a change, and with `b` the agent repo's `@`, the session's journal, is committed as it
stands. A failure after the first commit restores both repos from `jj op` snapshots.

### open

Open a cycle by making its bookmark first, on the work `@`, before the opening's record, ladder,
and bump are written, so every edit of the cycle is on its branch. [`commit
--opening`](#commit) then commits the opening on it.

```bash
vc-x1 open --title "feat: a cycle"            # feat-a-cycle, the title's slug
vc-x1 open --bookmark mine                    # a name of your own
vc-x1 open --title "feat: a cycle" --dry-run  # print the name, make nothing
```

`--title` is the bare cycle title, and the bookmark its slug, the anchor a heading of the title
gets: lowercase, `-` and `_` kept, each space a `-`, everything else dropped, so `feat: no trunk,
every target is named` names `feat-no-trunk-every-target-is-named`. `--bookmark` names it instead,
and one of the two is required. A name in use, locally or on `origin`, is refused, since a new one
would move or shadow it, and nothing else is: `@` may hold edits, which become the opening's, and
a `main` not where its `origin` was last fetched is a warning, a Land onto a target that moved
being refused anyway. The bookmark goes on `@`, so it follows the change through every snapshot and
the opening's commit. The agent repo gets none, being on `main` alone, and nothing is pushed. `-R`
is optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

### land

Land a cycle whose last commit is already made, on the machine: the agent `@` committed when the
cycle's commits name it, `--onto` fast-forwarded to `--source`, and the cycle's bookmark deleted,
every check made before anything moves. `--push` also publishes it, the work repo first, and
deletes the bookmark on `origin`, and refuses a push that would be forced, which `push` and
`squash-push` ask about. Without it `vc-x1 push -s b --bookmark <ONTO>` publishes, a
published cycle's bookmark left on `origin` for `delete-bookmark`. It is the Land of a closing made
without `--land`, or of a single-step commit, and the second half of `commit --closing ... --land`,

stands. A failure after the first commit restores both repos from `jj op` snapshots.

### open

Open a cycle by making its bookmark first, on the work `@`, before the opening's record, ladder,
and bump are written, so every edit of the cycle is on its branch. [`commit
--opening`](#commit) then commits the opening on it.

```bash
vc-x1 open --title "feat: a cycle"            # feat-a-cycle, the title's slug
vc-x1 open --bookmark mine                    # a name of your own
vc-x1 open --title "feat: a cycle" --dry-run  # print the name, make nothing
```

`--title` is the bare cycle title, and the bookmark its slug, the anchor a heading of the title
gets: lowercase, `-` and `_` kept, each space a `-`, everything else dropped, so `feat: no trunk,
every target is named` names `feat-no-trunk-every-target-is-named`. `--bookmark` names it instead,
and one of the two is required. A name in use, locally or on `origin`, is refused, since a new one
would move or shadow it, and nothing else is: `@` may hold edits, which become the opening's, and
a `main` not where its `origin` was last fetched is a warning, a Land onto a target that moved
being refused anyway. The bookmark goes on `@`, so it follows the change through every snapshot and
the opening's commit. The agent repo gets none, being on `main` alone, and nothing is pushed. `-R`
is optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

without `--land`, or of a single-step commit, and the second half of `commit --closing ... --land`,

optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

  are removed**, so `vc-x1 open` and `cycle --open` both make the bookmark, by the same code.

    stage's alone requires that stage's flag, so the parser makes the refusal.
- The record's edits are text in and text out, in `src/cycle/record.rs`, each file's new text
  planned before the bookmark is made.

  reads as an omission.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

Solution: a loader finds and reads the file and a parser takes text and
returns the schema, so a test hands the parser a string, and `main` gets
the schema from one call. See details in TODO.md.
```

The first paragraph states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes.
The second opens "Solution:" and ends with the pointer, and nothing names a file that the diff
already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". See details in
TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body names the cycle by its title and points at
its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

whose title is no rung's, so an unplanned rung gets its heading before its commit, a rung written
twice, a ladder whose first rung is not the cycle title plus " opening" or whose last is not it
plus " closing", and a line of the ladder already there that is not a rung, a left-margin `- `

        a single-step cycle, the closing squashed into its one commit: made\\n\\

        head, each a parent after @'s. --dead-end always makes a closing\\n\\
        commit, titled \\" dead-end closing\\". The ladder is rewritten, every\\n\\

        The acceptance check comes first, by hand, and again after.\\n\\n\\

assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)

```
'''
new='''vc-x1 cycle --commit --title "feat: one rung" --body @body.txt  # a work rung
vc-x1 cycle --close                                     # a ladder's closing, linear
vc-x1 cycle --close --trapezoid main                    # a merge, main its first parent
vc-x1 cycle --close --body @body.txt                    # a single-step cycle's one commit
```
'''
assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)
old='''no title or body. `--dry-run` prints the descriptions and commits nothing.
'''
new=old+'''
`--close [REV,...]` closes the cycle in progress from the work `@`, which is on the cycle's tip,
the bookmark on `@` or `@-`. The acceptance check is run first, by hand, and again after. The
branch's commit count is the cycle's shape, read and never asked:

- No commit, the work in `@`: a single-step cycle, its one commit made now from `@` under the bare
  cycle title.
- One commit, the opening: a single-step cycle too, the closing squashed into it. `@` is folded
  in, the title loses " opening", and the commit keeps its change id and its trailer, so its
  partner stands and the agent `@` is left for `push`.
- More: a ladder, whose closing is its own commit, the cycle title plus " closing", with
  `[closing] body` from the config, or a body naming the cycle and its record when the key is
  absent. `--dead-end` always makes it, titled " dead-end closing".

A single-step cycle's commit holds the work, so its `--body` is required, and `--default-body`
is the waiver, the pointer at the record. A `--title` or `--body` given is used as written.

A ladder's closing is linear by default, a plain commit on `@`'s own parents. `--trapezoid
<BOOKMARK>` makes it a merge whose first parent is the destination, read where it is now, so a
destination that moved is joined, and each `REV` listed is another head joined, a parent after
`@`'s own, so a bushy tree closes in one merge. A single-step cycle joins nothing and takes
neither.

The closing carries the record: the ladder is rewritten, every rung done, one unlinked rung for a
single-step cycle, and the `## In Progress` block moves to `## Closed`. Both files are put back
and the repo restored when the commit is not made. `-s` and `--push` are `--commit`'s.
'''
assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(t)

p='TODO.md'; t=open(p).read()
a=t.index("##### feat: cycle --close makes the closing"); b=t.index("##### feat: cycle --land advances the destination")
new='''##### feat: cycle --close makes the closing

The closing is `commit --closing <BM|REV> --onto <BOOKMARK>`, its parents and its shape implied.
`cycle --close [REV,...]` lists the heads joined, `@` when none is listed, and `--trapezoid <T>`
makes the destination the first parent. A single-step cycle's closing is squashed into its
opening, the title losing " opening" and the body required. A ladder's closing is its own commit,
its title and body defaulted. It moves the block to `## Closed`, and the acceptance check is the
first thing in closing, by hand.

- The closing is always made from the work `@`, which must be on the cycle's tip, so the detour
  `commit --closing` made around a tip elsewhere is gone: `jj new <bookmark>` puts `@` there.
- The count is of the cycle's branch, read as the ladder reads it, so the shape needs no
  destination, and only a trapezoid names one.
- A ladder's closing is linear unless `--trapezoid` or a head listed makes it a merge, which is
  the linear shape built, where `commit --closing` always merged. The agent-files still say a
  ladder lands as a trapezoid, so until **docs: the Cycle Protocol follows the cycle command**
  decides the default in the rules, this repo's closings pass `--trapezoid`.
  - The parents are the destination first, then `@`'s own, then each head listed, none twice.
- The single-step waiver is `--default-body`, the agent's name for it: the body is `[closing]
  body`, the pointer. `[closing] body` absent is no longer a refusal, a built-in body taking its
  place, as the opening's does.
- A `--title` given is the commit's title as written, not the bare cycle title, so no suffix is
  appended to it and none is refused.
- `--dead-end` is kept, always a closing commit.
- The ladder and the record move are written before the commit and put back when it is not made.
- After the closing `## In Progress` is empty, so `cycle --ladder` and `cycle --commit` have no
  cycle to read, and the Land reads the branch and not the record.
- Not done: the old closing's `--land` in the same invocation, which is the next rung's chain.

'''
t=t[:a]+new+t[b:]; open(p,'w').write(t)
EOF

1	//! Land: make a finished cycle permanent on its `--onto` bookmark. The agent `@` is
2	//! committed when the cycle's commits name it, the bookmark is
3	//! fast-forwarded to the cycle's last commit, and the cycle's bookmark
4	//! is deleted, all on the machine, every check made before anything
5	//! moves. `--push` also publishes, the work repo first and then the
6	//! agent repo, and deletes the bookmark on `origin`, and without it
7	//! `vc-x1 push` publishes.
8	//!
9	//! - [`plan`] refuses before anything is made: `--onto` is a local
10	//!   bookmark at its `origin` position, so the sync a Land begins with
11	//!   has nothing to bring, and the branch descends from it, so the tree
12	//!   landed is the reviewed one. The branch's other bookmarks are named
13	//!   as merged and left as they are.
14	//! - [`run`] lands what the plan names: a conflicted target is refused,
15	//!   the agent `@` is committed with one `ochid:` per work commit naming
16	//!   it, oldest first, the trailers the cycle's commits carry are updated
17	//!   by [`crate::trailers::update`], an older commit's `ocid:` and
18	//!   `pcid:` giving way to `orepo:`, `--onto` is fast-forwarded, and the cycle's bookmark is deleted, `--skip`
19	//!   keeping a side. A dry run makes every
20	//!   check and says each step, and does none: each step is its line and
21	//!   then the step behind `if !dry`, so a step added brings its dry-run
22	//!   line.
23	//!
24	//! `vc-x1 land -s b|p --source <BM|REV> --onto <BOOKMARK>` lands a cycle
25	//! whose last commit is already made, and `commit --closing ... --land`
26	//! plans its Land before the closing is made and runs it after, both
27	//! through these two.
28	//!
29	//! - `--source` names the cycle's last commit, a bookmark or a revision,
30	//!   and the cycle's bookmark by the rule [`cycle_bookmark`] states,
31	//!   `--closing`'s. Left out, it is the one local bookmark besides
32	//!   `--onto`, [`default_source`].
33	//! - `--onto` is any local bookmark `--source` descends from, so a
34	//!   bushy tree lands anywhere. Land only fast-forwards: a merge is
35	//!   `commit --closing`'s to make.
36	//! - `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks` deletes the bookmarks on the
37	//!   commits strictly between `--onto` and `--source`, the earlier
38	//!   cycles' of a stack landing together. Without it they are named as
39	//!   merged and kept, and a bookmark at the tip besides the cycle's is
40	//!   kept either way.
41	//! - The publish follows where the landed commit is: the work `@-`, whose pair
42	//!   may be unfinished, goes through `push`, which finishes it, and a
43	//!   commit below it, whose pair is finished, by its `--onto` bookmark pushed alone
44	//!   and the agent `main` published.

136	    /// Resolve the scope to the repo the Land moves bookmarks in.
137	    fn try_from(a: &LandArgs) -> Result<Self, String> {
138	        let repo = match &a.scope {
139	            RepoScope::Por => {
140	                let repos = crate::common::resolve_scoped_repos(&a.scope, a.repo.as_deref())
141	                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
142	                match repos.as_slice() {
143	                    [repo] => repo.clone(),
144	                    other => {
145	                        return Err(format!("land -s p: expected one repo, got {}", other.len()));
146	                    }
147	                }
148	            }
149	            RepoScope::Sides(sides) if sides.is_both() => {
150	                crate::pair::resolve_pair(a.repo.as_deref())
151	                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
152	                    .work
153	            }
154	            RepoScope::Sides(_) => {
155	                return Err(
156	                    "land: a work-only Land would publish trailers naming agent commits its \
157	                     agent half may not have published, and the agent repo alone has no cycle to \
158	                     land, so the scope is `-s b`, or `-s p` for a plain repo"
159	                        .into(),
160	                );
161	            }
162	        };
163	        Ok(LandParams {
164	            repo,
165	            scope: a.scope.clone(),
166	            source: a.source.clone(),
167	            onto: a.onto.clone(),
168	            skip: a.skip,
169	            delete_intermediate: a.delete_intermediate_bookmarks,
170	            push: a.push,
171	            dry_run: a.dry_run.value,
172	        })
173	    }

190	/// Entry point: resolve `--source` and the cycle's bookmark, plan the
191	/// Land, refusing before anything moves, and run it.
192	pub fn land(ctx: &mut Context, params: &LandParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
193	    debug!("land: enter {params:?}");
194	    let repo = params.repo.as_path();
195	    if !jj::local_bookmark_exists(repo, &params.onto)? {
196	        return Err(format!(
197	            "land: '{}' is not a local bookmark, and Land moves one",
198	            params.onto
199	        )
200	        .into());
201	    }
202	    let source = match &params.source {
203	        Some(s) => s.clone(),
204	        None => default_source(repo, &params.onto)?,
205	    };
206	    let tip = resolve_tip(repo, "land", &source)?;
207	    if jj::cid_of(repo, &params.onto)? == tip {
208	        return Err(format!(
209	            "land: '{}' is at '{source}' already, so there is nothing to land",
210	            params.onto
211	        )
212	        .into());
213	    }
214	    let bookmark = cycle_bookmark(repo, "land", "--source", &source, &params.onto, &tip)?;
215	    if bookmark.is_none() {
216	        info!(
217	            "land: no bookmark on the branch above '{}', so none is deleted",
218	            params.onto
219	        );
220	    }
221	    let plan = plan(
222	        repo,
223	        "land",
224	        params.onto.clone(),
225	        &tip,
226	        bookmark.as_deref(),
227	        params.skip,
228	        params.delete_intermediate,
229	    )?;
230	    run(
231	        ctx,
232	        repo,
233	        params.scope.clone(),
234	        &LandPlan {
235	            push: params.push,
236	            ..plan
237	        },
238	        &tip,
239	        &format!("'{source}'"),
240	        params.dry_run,
241	    )
242	}

244	/// `--source` left out: the one local bookmark besides `onto`, refused
245	/// with the list when there are several, since naming one settles it.
246	pub(crate) fn default_source(
247	    repo: &Path,
248	    onto: &str,
249	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
250	    let mut found = jj::local_bookmarks_at(repo, "bookmarks()")?;
251	    found.retain(|b| b != onto);
252	    match found.as_slice() {
253	        [one] => {
254	            info!("land: --source is '{one}', the one local bookmark besides '{onto}'");
255	            Ok(one.clone())
256	        }
257	        [] => Err(format!(
258	            "land: there is no local bookmark besides '{onto}', so there is nothing to land"
259	        )
260	        .into()),
261	        several => Err(format!(
262	            "land: there are several local bookmarks besides '{onto}', {}, so which is the \
263	             source is not known: name it, --source <BM|REV>",
264	            several.join(", ")
265	        )

294	/// The cycle's bookmark, the one a Land deletes, decided by `arg`, the
295	/// argument of `flag` that names the tip: a bookmark named is that one;
296	/// a revision means the current bookmark on the tip, else the nearest
297	/// parent's, above `onto`, several at that height refused with the
298	/// list, since naming one settles it, and none being none. The `onto`
299	/// bookmark itself is never the cycle's.
300	pub(crate) fn cycle_bookmark(
301	    repo: &Path,
302	    label: &str,
303	    flag: &str,
304	    arg: &str,
305	    onto: &str,
306	    tip: &str,
307	) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
308	    if arg != onto && jj::local_bookmark_exists(repo, arg)? {
309	        return Ok(Some(arg.to_string()));
310	    }
311	    let base = jj::cid_of(repo, onto)?;
312	    let mut found =
313	        jj::local_bookmarks_at(repo, &format!("heads(({base}..({tip})) & bookmarks())"))?;
314	    found.retain(|b| *b != onto);
315	    match found.len() {
316	        0 => Ok(None),
317	        1 => Ok(found.pop()),
318	        _ => Err(format!(
319	            "{label}: '{arg}' has several bookmarks at its nearest, {}, so which is the \
320	             cycle's is not known: name it, {flag} <BOOKMARK>",
321	            found.join(", ")
322	        )
323	        .into()),
324	    }
325	}

348	/// Plan a Land of the branch read up to `tip` onto `onto`, refusing
349	/// before anything is made. `bookmark` is the cycle's, deleted after,
350	/// and with `delete_intermediate` the bookmarks strictly between too.
351	pub(crate) fn plan(
352	    repo: &Path,
353	    label: &'static str,
354	    onto: String,
355	    tip: &str,
356	    bookmark: Option<&str>,
357	    skip: Option<Skip>,
358	    delete_intermediate: bool,
359	) -> Result<LandPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
360	    if !jj::local_bookmark_exists(repo, &onto)? {
361	        return Err(
362	            format!("{label}: '{onto}' is not a local bookmark, and Land moves one").into(),
363	        );
364	    }
365	    let onto_cid = jj::cid_of(repo, &onto)?;
366	    let remote = jj::remote_bookmark_targets(repo, "origin")?
367	        .get(&onto)
368	        .cloned();
369	    if remote.as_deref() != Some(onto_cid.as_str()) {
370	        return Err(format!(
371	            "{label}: '{onto}' is at {onto_cid} locally and {} on origin: sync first, \
372	             since a bookmark that moved stops a Land",
373	            remote.as_deref().unwrap_or("absent")
374	        )
375	        .into());
376	    }
377	    if !jj::matches(repo, &format!("{onto_cid} & ::({tip})"))? {
378	        return Err(format!(
379	            "{label}: the branch does not descend from '{onto}' at {onto_cid}, so \
380	             '{onto}' moved since the fork and the Land would carry a tree no validation saw: rebase \
381	             the branch onto it first"
382	        )
383	        .into());
384	    }
385	    let topic = bookmark.map(str::to_string);
386	    let others = |revset: &str| -> Result<Vec<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
387	        let mut found = jj::local_bookmarks_at(repo, revset)?;
388	        found.retain(|b| *b != onto && Some(b) != topic.as_ref());
389	        Ok(found)
390	    };
391	    let between = others(&format!("(({onto_cid}..({tip})) ~ ({tip})) & bookmarks()"))?;
392	    let mut merged = others(&format!("({tip}) & bookmarks()"))?;
393	    let intermediate = if delete_intermediate {
394	        between
395	    } else {
396	        merged.splice(0..0, between);
397	        Vec::new()
398	    };
399	    info!(
400	        "{label}: land onto '{onto}' at {onto_cid}, the cycle's bookmark {}",
401	        topic
402	            .as_deref()
403	            .map(|t| format!("'{t}'"))
404	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".into())
405	    );
406	    Ok(LandPlan {
407	        label,
408	        onto,
409	        onto_cid,
410	        topic,
411	        skip,
412	        intermediate,
413	        merged,
414	        push: false,
415	    })
416	}

418	/// The agent commit a Land makes: its description, the target's text
419	/// with one `ochid:` per commit from `onto_cid` to `target` that names
420	/// the agent `@`, oldest first, in the form each took. `None` when none
421	/// does, the cycle's pairs being made already. A commit above `target`
422	/// naming it is refused, since it would be left behind by the commit.
423	fn land_agent_desc(
424	    pair: &crate::pair::Pair,
425	    label: &str,
426	    onto_cid: &str,
427	    target: &str,
428	) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
429	    let work = pair.work.as_path();
430	    let agent_at = jj::chid_of(&pair.agent, "@")?;
431	    let names_agent_at = |rev: &str| -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
432	        Ok(extract_ochid_from_desc(&jj::desc_of(work, rev)?)
433	            .filter(|ochid| extract_bare_id(ochid) == agent_at))
434	    };
435	    for rev in jj::cids_of(work, &format!("({target})..@-"))? {
436	        if names_agent_at(&rev)?.is_some() {
437	            return Err(format!(
438	                "{label}: {rev}, above what is landed, also names the agent @ {agent_at}, which a \
439	                 Land commits, so land the line up to it"
440	            )
441	            .into());
442	        }
443	    }
444	    let mut values = Vec::new();
445	    for rev in jj::cids_of(work, &format!("{onto_cid}..({target})"))? {
446	        if names_agent_at(&rev)?.is_some() {
447	            values.push(jj::chid_of(work, &rev)?);
448	        }
449	    }
450	    if values.is_empty() {
451	        return Ok(None);
452	    }
453	    let desc = jj::desc_of(work, target)?;
454	    let text = without_trailer_lines(&desc).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
455	    Ok(Some(with_ochids(&text, repo_url_for(work)?, &values)))
456	}

458	/// Land what `land` plans onto `target`, named `what` in messages:
459	/// refuse a conflicted target, commit the agent `@` when the cycle's
460	/// commits name it, fast-forward `onto` to it, delete the cycle's
461	/// bookmark, `--skip` keeping a side, and with `land.push` publish it,
462	/// `scope` saying which repos, and delete on `origin` too. A dry run
463	/// makes every check and says each step, and does none.
464	pub(crate) fn run(
465	    ctx: &mut Context,
466	    repo: &Path,
467	    scope: RepoScope,
468	    land: &LandPlan,
469	    target: &str,
470	    what: &str,
471	    dry: bool,
472	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
473	    let LandPlan {
474	        label,
475	        onto,
476	        onto_cid,
477	        topic,
478	        skip,
479	        intermediate,
480	        merged,
481	        push,
482	    } = land;
483	    let push = *push;
484	    // Local, the remote side is left whatever is asked, so `--skip
485	    // local`, which would delete only the remote, deletes nothing.
486	    let keep = match (skip, push) {
487	        (Some(Skip::Both), _) | (Some(Skip::Local), false) => None,
488	        (Some(Skip::Local), true) => Some(Some(crate::delete_bookmark::Keep::Local)),
489	        (Some(Skip::Remote), _) | (None, false) => Some(Some(crate::delete_bookmark::Keep::Remote)),
490	        (None, true) => Some(None),
491	    };
492	    // Checks run in both modes, so a dry run refuses what a Land would.
493	    if jj::matches(repo, &format!("({target}) & conflicts()"))? {
494	        return Err(format!(
495	            "{label}: {what} is conflicted, so it is not landed: resolve it, then \
496	             land it with `vc-x1 move-bookmark --bookmark {onto} --target {target}` and \
497	             `vc-x1 push`"
498	        )
499	        .into());
500	    }
501	    // Each step's line, then the step, which a dry run leaves undone.
502	    let tag = if dry { " [dry-run]" } else { "" };
503	    // The work @-'s pair may be unfinished, which push finishes. A
504	    // commit below it has a finished pair, so its `--onto` bookmark goes alone.
505	    let at_work_head = jj::matches(repo, &format!("({target}) & @-"))?;
506	    let pair = match scope {
507	        RepoScope::Por => None,
508	        RepoScope::Sides(_) => Some(crate::pair::resolve_pair(Some(repo))?),
509	    };
510	    let agent_desc = match &pair {
511	        Some(pair) => land_agent_desc(pair, label, onto_cid, target)?,
512	        None => None,
513	    };
514	    if let (Some(pair), Some(desc)) = (&pair, &agent_desc) {
515	        info!(
516	            "{label}:{tag} commit the agent @ {} as the partner, in {}:\n{desc}",
517	            jj::chid_of(&pair.agent, "@")?,
518	            pair.agent.display()
519	        );
520	        if !dry {
521	            let snapshot = crate::pair::Snapshot::take(&pair.agent)?;
522	            let made = ctx
523	                .session(&pair.agent)?
524	                .commit(desc)
525	                .and_then(|_| ctx.session(&pair.agent)?.bookmark_set("main", "@-"));
526	            if let Err(e) = made {
527	                snapshot.restore(label, e.as_ref());
528	                return Err(e);
529	            }
530	        }
531	    }
532	    // By change id, since restamping a commit's trailers changes its SHA.
533	    let target_chid = jj::chid_of(repo, target)?;
534	    if let Some(pair) = &pair {
535	        crate::trailers::update(
536	            ctx,
537	            pair,
538	            &crate::trailers::Update {
539	                label,
540	                revset: &format!("{onto_cid}..({target})"),
541	                add: false,
542	                dry,
543	            },
544	        )?;
545	    }
